description: Create a BST iterator that can move forward and backward through inorder values. Example 1: for a tree with inorder [3, 7, 9, 15, 20], next returns 3 then 7, and prev returns 3. Example 2: after moving to the last element, hasNext is false while hasPrev remains true. Constraints: the tree is nonempty and all keys are unique.
intuition: Materializing the inorder sequence turns bidirectional iteration into cursor movement.

brute_force.approach: Recompute inorder traversal from the root for each next or prev operation.

optimal.approach: Build one inorder list and maintain the index of the current element.

edge_cases: The cursor begins before the first value.
prev is only called when hasPrev is true.
